caption:
Paint color: “London Stone” by Farrow and Ball

We first painted our living room “Pigeon” by Farrow & Ball within a year of moving in. And we loved it. It gave a tall, white, living room a lot of character. 4 years later, In 2025 our living room underwent a considerable renovation, that included installing 4 new skylights, rich wooden beams, built-in shelves, a window seat, and lots of custom trim among other things. Choosing the new paint color to complete our vision was no small task, but it all paid off. London Stone is historic, timeless, and just the right amount of moody, modern traditional I craved.

caption:
Hello all - Chris jumping in for a moment. Last week during dinner, one of our daughters expressed some anxiety at the idea of having a baby. The pain, the discomfort - it seemed like an impossible task to her. Jules shared a little about her experience, saying “Nobody is telling you you have to have kids. But I hope you don’t let the fact that it’s difficult be the reason you don’t. Because it’s so much more wonderful than it is difficult.” 

I remember the days leading up to Greta’s birth. Julia was noticeably nervous - just unsure of how it was going to go or how she would know when it was time. But the second her water broke, I saw her change. And that change has continued, day in and day out, for over 16 years now. I’ve only ever been able to attempt to keep up. 

I’ve never known someone more capable, driven, and hard working. But across everything she does, Jules absolutely shines as a mother. She loves and nurtures her daughters in exactly the ways they need her to, and helps them navigate their challenges so capably. It’s the greatest privilege of my life to be part of it. We love you, Julia. All our hearts. Happy Mother’s Day.

caption: Maybe you do know, maybe you don’t, BUT interior designers don’t just pick paint and fabric….we’re also deep in architectural drawings, millwork details, and often select every single finish in a home. One of my favorite tricks for adding light AND architectural interest….TRANSOM WINDOWS!! I’ve been known to love ’em….but what are they and WHY are they my jam, you ask??? Welp, a transom window is basically just a pane of glass installed directly above a door or another window, separated by a horizontal beam (called, you guessed it, a transom!) They add natural light and architectural interest, and in my opinion, really upgrade a boring old opening!! Soooo here are a few I’ve designed over the years, from pantries to entryways. Ok consider yourself learned!!! HA! What should I highlight next??! // ?? shadedeggesphotography

caption: I am sure there are a LOT of folks who would see the “before” bathroom pics and think it was perfect….. but here is the deal, my clients didn’t think it was perfect and so Amber Interiors entered the chat. Luckily we had really good bones to work with over at #clientfromgoodtogreat so we started there. We didn’t need two massive showers, and we didn’t need to take a bath for all the neighbors to see. We tackled the layout and made all the awkward stuff more functional, and of course, super beautiful. How, you ask?? Welp, it included moving the tub to the center of the space with a wall and hiding the shower behind it for a bit more privacy. That gave us the room to make bigger vanities and add more storage!! The whole bathroom now feels really intentional, much more usable, and aesthetically aligned with the client’s vision. Renovations are a special kind of beast, so l love when it all works out seamlessly like this stunner. // ?? shadedeggesphotography

My third book, INTERIORS, documents my design process (with a capital P!) and tours 9 homes my team and I have created since 2020. Sooo I thought it’d be fun to take you through those six steps here on the ‘gram! What say you???

+ PONDER: The project is locked in and confirmed. Let the inspiration and daydreaming begin! 

+ PLAY: We get the party started by strategizing schemes, pairings, patterns, and effects.

+ PROCURE: We source the perfect pieces for each project – whether it be custom, new, or vintage. 

+ PATIENCE/PANIC: Some projects more than others, but every home has its hiccups. Trust the process…

+ PULL IT TOGETHER: The vision becomes reality and install is finally happening! 

+ PRIDE: Nothing matches the feeling of seeing all your hard work pay off and leaving an indelible mark on a property and client. 

Annnnd that’s all I’ll share for now….pre-order a copy for the rest of the dirty deets. No, really….link in bio and stories! // #crappyiphonepicsaremyjam

caption:
I’m often asked how I style shelves, or as we like to call it around here….a shelfie! Soooo let’s break it down a bit, shall we?? 

+ Book stacks and artwork go in first. These are your anchors…your focal points. The goal is to set up a little visual ping-pong. You know, a little something over here, a little something over there, all while paying attention to consistency in color tones and scale. The trick is that you want your eyes to be drawn to multiple things without ever feeling overwhelmed. This is your base layer to build upon.

+ Now layer it up! Add in items of different shapes, heights, and textures to add depth and dimension. Orrrrr consider a light (a picture light or the Calla Bookshelf Lamp I designed with fourhandsfurniture would be fab here…) 

+ Lastly, fill in the gaps with those finishing touches! I like to create small groupings – placing items of similar colors or vibes together for added visual interest and impact.

Remember dudes, it’s all about what floats your boat and there’s not a specific formula that works every time. It should reflect YOU and the vibes you’re trying to create, these are just a few things I go by. Anywho, I hope that helped….buh-bye!

Mood boards are a key part of how every single one of my shoots comes to life, so let’s build one together using AdobeFirefly Boards! ???

When I’m planning a shoot, my inspiration can come from so many different places: props, locations, lighting, a color palette, or posing ideas. caption:
One shoot, five different moods with NikonUSA Picture Controls ?

I’ve been loving using Nikon Picture Controls in my shoots lately because they let me preview different looks in camera as I’m shooting. Seeing a look come to life in camera can even change how I frame or compose the shot, while also helping me visualize the final image on location before I even get to the edit.

One of my favorite parts is how flexible they are. You’re not locked into just one look, and you can adjust things like sharpening, contrast, and brightness or control the overall effect strength to fine-tune everything. And if I want to keep adjusting it later on, I can still make changes in Nikon’s NX Studio.

Nikon Z series cameras include 20 Creative Picture Controls, so it’s easy to take one setup and give it a totally different feel depending on the mood.

Lately I’ve been using Linktr.ee to get a bigger picture of what’s resonating across my Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, and it’s been such a helpful part of my creative process. With their new insights and social analytics, I can ask more specific questions about trends and what I should lean into creatively, which has helped me go into new shoots with a clearer plan from the start. 

I can also better understand the best days and times to share my work, so the ideas I’m most excited about have a better chance of reaching more of you. One of the setups I wanted to revisit in a new way was the acrylic sheet and colored gels, but this time I decided to switch it up by painting shapes to shoot through instead. I love exploring ideas that still feel creative and personal to me, while using these tools to shape the overall direction of what I create so it feels more intentional.

Warm vs. cool photo challenge: hotel room edition ??

We came together once again to do a shoot using the same camera, model, and location, but this time working with different color temperatures. We brought our own lighting into this hotel room and shot with warm + cool tones to see how a shift in color (along with our own personal styles) could completely change the feeling of the same scene.

We both shot with the NikonUSA Z5II and the NIKKOR Z 24-70mm f/2.8 S lens ??

Let us know… do you usually use more reds or blues when you’re shooting? #photography #nikoncreators #colorhunt

caption:
3 Creative Portrait Tips I swear by when shooting with NikonUSA

1?? Lighting
To avoid my images feeling flat… I always start by lighting my subject first, then layer in additional lights around my subject for separation and depth.

2?? Color
Warmer vs. cooler tones can instantly change the vibe of your scene. And if you don’t have full control over the temperature of your lights, you can always adjust it in camera by changing your white balance!

3?? Creative Picture Controls
To save time in the edit, apply Creative Picture Controls or Imaging Recipes in camera. You get a stylized look in real time, so you’re shooting closer to your final look while on set. I’m using Cinematic Blue, Teal & Orange, and Neon Glow here, all available on Nikon’s Imaging Cloud?

Gear I’m Using: Nikon Z5II + NIKKOR Z 50mm f/1.2 S lens ??

If you’re in Las Vegas anytime until January 9th, be sure to check out Lexar in the Central Hall at booth 20234 to see their latest releases and what’s next in the world of memory!

caption:
My parents used to say, “Of course we’re worried. There’s no word in Chinese for what you do.” As the kid of Chinese immigrants, I was told there were only three careers: doctor, lawyer, or professor. Climbing bum was not on that list. When I finished college, I was sure these traditional expectations didn’t fit me, and I decided to make up my own way through the world. I would spend my twenties drifting between climbing destinations and living out of a stubborn 1989 Subaru Loyale.

It was not the graduate program my mom and dad had hoped for me. Thankfully, my parents also instilled in me the work ethic and confidence to strive for a life I didn’t even know I wanted — the life I discovered on sweeping granite walls, desert towers, and knife-edge ridges.

Along the way, I found a second family in the adventurers who seek out the world’s wildest places and devote their lives to accomplishing what others have never dared. The members of this tribe became my most cherished friends, partners, and mentors. Every person I’ve climbed with has helped shape me into who I am today.

Photos by cheynelempe dougworkman conrad_anker mikeylikesrocks and gpmartinphoto

caption:
The Ennedi Desert in Chad looks like a larger, more spectacular version of Arizona and Utah’s Monument Valley, with immense towers, arches, and canyons spread across a vast expanse of sand. Unlike Monument Valley, it’s usually 110 degrees F during the “cool” season. Summer temperatures can reach 140.

Getting to the Ennedi required five days of off-road driving. Because our Land Cruisers had no air conditioning, we kept the windows open. It felt like having a giant hair dryer blasting in your face. 

Piero, our guide who had once been a climber himself, knew what kind of journey we sought. He brought us to the area’s most dramatic formations, including the spindly Arch of Bishekele.

It may be unforgiving, but the Ennedi holds the allure of all deserts - the austerity of the landscape, the cool quiet nights, and the endless stars to fall asleep beneath.

caption:

Chapter 2 - Another Planet

There’s nothing like hitting the ground running.. or in this case bikepacking.. in a completely new place. Everything is foreign & nothing is comfortable - it’s exactly how I like my adventures.

Bikepacking in Iceland is always a slight sufferfest. Any positive outlook at the start of each day receives a barrage of attacks from unexpected challenges - tire punctures, mechanical issues, bad weather… mostly Wind. Iceland’s variable terrain and temperamental climate don’t make it easier.. but its wilderness huts make it digestible.

At the end of a trying day we step into a warm, dry space where we can finally relax after hours in the saddle. For Jabba therealhikingviking , like many, its the carrot on the stick to get through each day and recover enough to willingly face tomorrow. Its a miracle what a warm meal and dry socks can do for you..

caption:
Brought to you by AI.. I guess.

Unfortunately this is a standard response to many creators’ posts now. After putting so much effort into scouting a location to best capture its mystifying nature and then share it with the world.. its labelled artificially generated. Maybe it’s a badge of honor that we’ve done our job so well people can’t believe it’s real..

The more time spent online distorts your ability to determine for yourself what’s actually fake and what’s just a rad spot. It’s probably time to go outside and take a hike.

#takeahike mammut mammutna

caption:
There isn’t a single piece of clothing I’ve worn more in my life than my rapha Brevet bibs. Countless days in the saddle in multiple countries collecting the Blood, Sweat and actual Tears that only ultra distance racing can provide. Happy to say it’s the only piece of kit that has been a no-brainer when meticulously packing and prepping for a long adventure by bike. As seen here in Kyrgyzstan last summer where the same pair of bibs was worn for 25 days of riding. 

Their new Brevet collection just launched & it has me stoked for all the sufferfests to come. I’ll be heading to Germany end of May for a big ol ride through the mountains with RCC. see ya Out There.

thanks joelbarger_ for the legendary photos !

caption:
I’m stoked to introduce 

‘Field Notes: Iceland’ - a new mini series we cut specifically for instagram.

Chapter 1 - The Setup

Id been sitting on this route for 4 years after mapsoficeland built it for me. I wanted something remote and super challenging moving North to South, but digestible enough to bring a hardy first timer along - enter therealhikingviking , aka Jabba. 

The route was a perfect right of passage for Jabba into the world of nordic bikepacking, but also a rad way for him to experience Iceland for the first time. It’s not a typical first visit somewhere.. traveling in the highlands and near the eastern rim of Vatnajokull glacier is.. chaotic, especially with the variable weather of Icelandic summers. That unpredictable wildness only made for a more memorable adventure. 

huge shout out to ridepriority for supporting this project! Jabba was riding the 600ADX , purpose built for rugged adventure like this.

caption:
9 months ago I was standing on the world’s tallest suspension bridge weeks before its opening. I was attempting to shoot the behemoth subject and the thought came to me… “I have no idea what I’m doing.”

I’ll admit I was baffled at how life had led me here, but it had been years since I had tried to document anything manmade and of this scale. Shooting architecture was a foreign concept to me, but there I was hooked onto 3 inch safety wires documenting the Huajiang Canyon Bridge. 

I was disoriented walking on a cable suspended over 2000 feet in the air - the Empire State building could fit between me and the valley floor. Electricians continued wiring around me.. unfazed. I, on the other hand, was mesmerized by the sprawling landscape below my feet. Moving just a few steps required a constant adjustment of safety gear & scrutiny over the radio if i wasn’t focused enough on my cable management while I attempted to shoot photos leaning over the edges and maxing out the cables length…. definitely out of my element, but in those few hours I spent on the cables the more comfortable it got. Eventually I was finding leading lines, making shapes, playing more with composition & light amongst this massive structure. 

Shot on assignment with natgeo in Guizhou, China

caption:
Ripping through the desert with the boys never disappoints!

This was my goal 8 weeks post shoulder surgery.. back on my bike riding with friends. I had this Anzo-Borrego loop bookmarked - a chill trip to start back with, but rad enough to make a cool birthday ride.

Its geology keeps the riding interesting - canyons riddled with erosion exposing trippy textures and formations. Deep gulches cut through sedimentary layers revealing fossils buried for millennia. Tectonic movements formed its dramatic rock structures millions of years ago.. riding here is a physical tour of the Earth’s geological history. 

Such a sick way to usher in a new decade of life.. surrounded by a good crew of friends always down bivy in the desert. Cheers boys!

caption:
Sure, what’s another hobby?

I find a lot of joy comes with being a beginner again.. No pressure to perform or achieve anything huge yet. Just acting as a sponge for any information I can soak up.

Fly fishing always seems to be a rabbit hole that never ends.. A forever search for the perfect presentation, the best knots, casting strategy and choosing the right fly.. That’s part of the fun of course for a student learning from other people’s lifelong passion.

I spent these hours standing out on the Breiddalsa in Iceland’s Eastfjords. My feet numb and my face windburned but I’m stoked. It’s about the devotion to a craft that fosters a deeper connection to the environment. A new perspective.. and a new reason to get outside.

caption:
Ever have those Indiana Jones moments?

The stoic expressions painting the guide’s face was a subtle cause for concern after warnings of vipers inhabiting the cave below … let’s just say close toed shoes were mandatory. 

Rappelling into Shuanghe Cave in China felt like dropping into an old movie set - completely enveloped in the mist, no real sense of the sheer size of the cavern or our exit plan. Seemed like you could park a 737 in there…

A scientist accompanied us to identify any new species of animals living in this remote cave tucked in the Guizhou province… getting stoked when we stumbled across a chubby tadpole swimming in the underground river. We finally hit daylight after navigating over a mile of cave -  requiring a heinous combination of canyoneering, wading, and paddle boarding out via river.  I do in fact, hate snakes. 

Shot on assignment for natgeo alongside my assistant joelbarger_ 

Kit - sonyalpha a1 II with 16-35mm F2.8 GM II and 24-70mm F2.8 GM II

I’ll be in Boston the next few days at the sonyalpha Creative Space on the Road talking shop and signing copies of Out There. Come hang !

caption:
While traveling Guizhou, China with natgeo , I had Fanjinshan Temple bookmarked - it Mystified me. 

Not only for the marvel of its architectural achievement, but by the WHY of it all. There are certainly easier places to put a Buddhist temple, but the monks in the 7th century chose the top of this rock spire. There’s a clear intentionality in that decision, as well as in the design of the temple itself. With it being so far removed from society below, it’s as if any worldly problem couldn’t follow us up here. All there was to focus on was the here and now. 

Every block of stone, wood beam, and iron tile hauled up the almost 9,000 narrow steps it takes to reach the summit - a gargantuan undertaking. A simple misstep and I would have found myself dropping over a cliff’s edge into the void below, and I wasn’t holding any massive objects. I was baffled by the unwavering faith required of the monks to do this, but also in their technical ability to build a temple withstanding centuries of constant barrage from harsh winds. Their unshakable belief in Buddhist teachings was tangible as I walked through this holy site. 

Places like this give me the ultimate perspective reset - a refounded sense of wonder in the boundlessness of the human spirit and the natural world, and a gentle reminder to slow down and take it all in.

caption:
Keith was always an elusive character - you never really knew when he would show up. Even if you did see him he’d probably be surfing a wood plank he just shaped, or paddling a big gun into fog toward some outer reef on a scary swell. But that was before I got to really travel with Keith and understand that for him it has only ever been about just being in the water. 

When we started working together, he urged me to realize that the craft didn’t matter. For him, discovering waves in backcountry Russia, towing maxed out Mavericks or competing at Pipeline in bodysurfing were just as cool as they served the same purpose of getting him in the ocean. As the person who taught me how to bodysurf somewhere down in rural Mexico, this mindset gave me the confidence to also feel justified sitting in the line up without a board.. just a pair of fins.

While a man of few words and not afraid of a good time either, Keith was always someone who would make the most of any situation no matter where you ended up in the world. A few of those situations we shared and some even left a few good scars and stories. Needless to say, Keith was the Swiss Army knife you wanted in any situation.

Alright I’ll stop embarrassing him now :)

caption:
It’s hard not to recognize this tour as a unique occurrence. Cold temps sustained across multiple days following a storm create a snowpack not often found in the western Sierra. A snow pit solidified our intent to get into every line we could. With powder demanding our attention, no roadblock was too big as we excitedly started a 14 mile ski tour with sleds full of food in waist deep snow - the normally delightful skin track was a distant memory. One night was spent huddled around an outhouse toilet for warmth and another in the clear open skies with a view of Half Dome and perfect snow. This normally moderate Glacier Point tour became a memorable epic. Earn your turns, as they say. 

A good time some years back with kcdeane and _ryanhill_

caption:
One of my favorite challenges of photography is shooting at night. The potential for an epic shot, so long as you answer the difficult questions. Without the sun doing the leg work, how do I find the lighting I’m looking for? How do I utilize the cold lighting already available to me? How do I sync these elements to create the contrast I’m looking for? Often you already have the answers, whether that be a longer exposure and wide open aperture, or just adding an extra log on the fire.

Shot on sonyalpha A7S II at a 3 second exposure, ISO 5000, Aperture 1.4

The finer details matter! 

Put in the work before the trip to know the in’s and out’s of where you are going. Take it from me, the guy who was detained for not knowing that walkie-talkies were prohibited in Cuba prior to its reopening to Americans. Or when an incorrect visa entry date into Russia got me detained for a few days. Do the research and prepare accordingly so you can deal with the fun issues, rather than the stressful ones.

caption:
I stood on the beach just 50 ft from the waters edge for hours staring into the backlit lineup… the reflection on the water and offshore wind whipping sand into the sky battered my vision leaving my eyes blurred, dry and irritated as if full of sand. The only remedy was a thick gel like eye goop that helped restore just enough sight to surf another day. While not in my eyes, sand certainly was everywhere else, finding its way into every orifice it could. In my eyes, between my teeth, and in my sheets at the end of the day. Unfortunately, no remedy for this one.

A low frequency, undeniably unique wave dependent on weather windows, cyclone patterns, and luck. Unwavering commitment to a raw experience; a prerequisite for finding yourself here at the opportune moment. Dylan Graves exhibits his composure as a sand bottom tube doubles up on him.

I’ve been working with outdooroutreach for 5 years and their mission to connect youth with nature and the experiences the outdoors offer. But not everyone has that mentor and that’s where outdooroutreach comes into play.

I was able to partner with ensorings on a ring inspired by iceland with 10% proceeds donated to outdooroutreach . Whether you’re chasing mountain tops with strangers, following the tide of the ocean or just moving through the rhythm of your day, these silicone rings are a quiet nod to adventure. A product to carry stories and celebrate the adventures we strive to create with the people we enjoy doing it with.

caption:
Life behind the scenes through the lens of my phone during my time in Guizhou, China. Such an awesome opportunity to adventure to that side of the world to host a natgeo TV show.

As much as I miss rappelling into the depths of the Shuanghe Cave, kayaking the Gaoguo River, and having a bridge-side cup of coffee on the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge, I’ll always appreciate the moments that help me grow as an individual and professional. As much fun as it was, there came personal challenges too.

It takes a different approach to photograph subjects that don’t require movement; Specifically, food and architecture. These subjects are outside of my normal expertise, but I’ve learned they ask for patience in a different way. Using leading lines, playing with shapes, and applying basic composition techniques that help frame the image. It’s less about chasing the moment and more about shaping it…

caption:
When a bodysurfer dolphins through a wave, there’s no telling where they’ll surface and emerge. A split second of uncertainty, shooting relatively blind and trusting instinct over sight.

I love that about moments like this shot. It’s nearly impossible to recreate being primarily dependent on the centrifugal force of the ocean. A motion you can’t control or rely on.. simply right place, right time and trusting that instinct.

Captured during the making of the film, Come Hell or High Water: The Plight of the Torpedo People, a film rooted in the purity of connection to the ocean and the timeless art of bodysurfing.

caption:
18 years ago, on a remote stretch of sand in the North Pacific of Christmas Island, a young Chris Burkard finds himself completely unprepared for his first real taste of a tropical adventure…

A handful of stories live within those early frames captured by my longtime friend michael.kew but one in particular sticks; A full circle moment. I would have never guessed 18 years later I’d be working with pelican . Before the story even knew what it would become years later, it’s like those cases were always there listening and watching…

Checkout The Case Chronicles on their website and what it’s all about! I look forward to reading all the wild case stories..

The first rule of landscape photography: Never approach a subject or a place thinking that you’re going to walk right up and make the best photo you’ve ever shot. Instead, ask yourself, What do I want to see?

A landscape artist has to create the depth on the canvas, create the distance of the mountains and the purple shadows and the orange sunset, all within the four borders of a painting. With a camera, you’re doing the same thing. You decide what goes into your picture..

caption:
Today, we honour courage

On 9 August 1956, more than 20,000 women from all walks of life marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria, standing together against unjust laws in South Africa. Their footsteps echoed a message that still resonates nearly seven decades later: “You strike a woman, you strike a rock.”

National Women’s Day is a reminder of the resilience, dignity and quiet strength that has shaped South Africa through a difficult and painful history.

At The Royal Portfolio, we are deeply privileged to work alongside remarkable women who embody that same spirit every day. 

Happy Women’s Day.
May we continue to walk forward together. With courage, compassion and hope.

From the Bush to the Classroom: Inspiring Africa’s Next Generation of Conservationists 

Dean Carlisle, founder of lessons.in.conservation is on a mission to build a conservation-minded generation across Southern and East Africa. From inspiring schoolchildren to training hospitality staff, Dean and his team are creating ripple effects that spark real change — one lesson, one conversation, and one connection at a time.

The Royal Portfolio recently welcomed Dean for a series of workshops with our teams, deepening our shared commitment to conservation, education, and community engagement.

It’s a powerful reminder that protecting the planet isn’t just the job of conservationists — it’s a collective responsibility. And meaningful impact often begins with small, local actions that spread outward.

Read more about Dean’s vision and our growing partnership in our latest blog, link in bio.

In Honour of a Legend

Our new tented camp at Royal Malewane is named after the late Wilson Masiya, one of only eight master trackers worldwide and a cherished member of the extended Royal Portfolio family.

After working as a tracker in Kruger National Park in the 1990s, Wilson soon gained a reputation as one of the best in the Greater Kruger. His strength of spirit and intimate knowledge of the bush made him a natural choice to join The Royal Portfolio team when the Biden family opened Royal Malewane in 1999.

Nature has a way of creating connections, and when an 18-year-old Juan Pinto went to Thornybush Nature Reserve fresh out of school to become a ranger, he had the good fortune to start working with Wilson Masiya. This brought together two men from different backgrounds whose kinship would span nearly two decades. Their partnership was legendary, and their deep bond and shared reverence for the wilderness shaped the ethos of Royal Malewane’s guiding experience.

Wilson Masiya sadly passed away in 2015. The Royal Portfolio team wanted to honour his memory in a special way. Our new tented offering, Masiya’s Camp, will be launched as a fitting tribute to his significant impact and enduring legacy. Masiya’s story endures through the ethos he helped create at Royal Malewane, living on in the memories of his loved ones, those he mentored, and within the tracker family.

Juan Pinto, Head of Conservation at Royal Malewane, continues to carry this legacy forward alongside our dedicated team.

Big smiles and pure joy filled the air at Wes-Eind Primary as 100 eager Grade 1 learners received their brand-new backpacks, each thoughtfully packed with stationery supplies and water bottles. This special moment, made possible by The Royal Portfolio Foundation, marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter in their school journey.

Every January, the La Residence team prepares these backpacks to ensure that each child starts their first year of primary school equipped with all the stationery they need. For families who may not be able to afford these essentials, this initiative helps ease the burden on parents while setting these young scholars up for success.

The team had the privilege of delivering the backpacks this year, and the children’s joy and excitement were truly contagious!

Giving Tuesday is a powerful reminder of the impact we can create when we come together with kindness and purpose. At The Royal Portfolio Foundation, we are deeply committed to uplifting local communities, protecting South Africa’s precious wildlife, and fostering a sustainable future for generations to come. This work is rooted in a deep love for the places we call home. 

Through our partnerships with communities, we provide education, healthcare, and skills development, empowering individuals to build brighter futures. At the same time, our conservation programmes work tirelessly to safeguard endangered wildlife and restore fragile ecosystems, ensuring the natural beauty of South Africa remains vibrant and protected.

Every contribution matters, and every action brings us closer to a future where communities thrive and nature flourishes. Together, we can leave a legacy of hope.

caption:
There’s always a lot of chatter online this time of year about the importance of getting kids outside to play.
?????????
I’m not here to discount the benefits of kids in nature, but I would like to gently remind folks that access to outdoor play is often out of someone’s control.

Guilting, shaming, or adding stress to families about where their children play doesn’t benefit anyone.

As we head into summer breaks in the northern hemisphere, please remember that ANY play time you can provide your child with is beneficial.

Play is play, and kids need it, whether it happens inside or out.

caption:
After a long, exhausting, rewarding year of work… I finally get to say:

Eight brand-new units of my elementary program are here ??

Comment PROGRAM to learn more ??

I couldn’t be more excited about this new set of units. I promise they were worth the wait. They’re innovative, they’re interactive, they’re incredible. From gargoyles to gravity, troglobites to telegrams… so much learning awaits.

And with these new units comes a new name for the program: Offshoots.

Offshoots is identical to Branches: the same framework, look and feel, and enchanting thematic units so families can learn together.

The only real change? A new name and a new shop. If you own Branches, those first 8 units were rolled under this new brand name.

ALL 16 UNITS ARE NOW AVAILABLE AS INDIVIDUAL UNITS OR YOU CAN BUNDLE THEM FOR A DISCOUNT.

Each Offshoots unit covers what I call the “discovery subjects”: science, social studies, language arts, and fine arts through interconnected, cross-cutting lessons. 
There are currently 16 units available, and each includes:

??A four week deep dive with step-by-step detailed lesson plans
??Thoughtfully created printables (hand made by me)
??Vetted multimedia links for immersive learning
??Hands-on activities to keep the magic of learning alive

Offshoots is a homeschool program, but it’s also a summer break program, an evenings together program, and a “my kid is obsessed with rocks” program.

Foundational knowledge, building memories, and cultivating a love of learning matter - no matter how your family does school.

Learning together is how my family builds camaraderie. It’s an easy way to connect. It’s an entry point to create shared moments together.

Taking a deep dive into a topic, as simple as that sounds, can give your family something that’s yours, together. 

I’m so proud of this program and so excited to see where this learning takes your family ??

caption:
Need something random? ??????
?????????
Let your kids paint ice cubes. It’s unexpected and something fun to reset the mood.
?????????
Set up: 
-ice cubes
-washable tempera paint

That’s it. Kids will keep coming back to this as the ice melts ?? but why bother setting this up?
?????????
Because something easy like this helps shift the mood. If things aren’t going great, it’s a long afternoon, the kids are fighting, no one can find their play… a set up like this can change the vibes.
?????????
I don’t set things out like this to be “wonder parent.” I set them out because we need something to do, anew thing to focus us, a shift in energy. I’m blowing the Nintendo cartridge. I’m hitting reset.
????????? 
Activities are a tool I found to help in my parenting. I keep ideas like this in my back pocket and pull them out when we need it.
?????????
Save this for the next long afternoon ??

caption:
I never feel bad for what I can or can’t give to each child.
?????????
Oh and as for my middle, she always has always had a companion and has a *slightly* more experienced parent. It all evens out.
?????????
We worry up and down about what we can or can’t give our children. It’s hard enough when we are comparing ourselves to the rest of the world through the social media window, but even harder when we start to compare from child to child in our own families, too.
?????????
If this has been weighing on your heart, please take a minute today and work to shift that perspective.
?????????
I know that’s a tall ask, but try this: Instead of looking at what you can’t give your child, look at what you do give or what they get. There’s individual greatness being given no matter how a family is structured.
????????? ?????????
Here’s how it sounds for me ??
?????????
My oldest is paving the way. He had one-on-one time with me and he gets to go first. He knows how to teach others and share learning with them. 
?????????
My middle never known life alone. She’s always had a friend. Her parents had one round of experience under their belts and are a little wiser. She learns skills from her older sibling, and also has someone she’s the big kid to. 
?????????
My youngest has always had a loud house. His parents were the most experienced and they knew how to support him. He has two guides in life and knows how to advocate for himself (maybe too well ??).
?????????
Three kids. Same parents. Different lives. And that’s a good thing if you let it be one.
?????????
Take a minute today and reflect on the positives of your child’s life. Focus on releasing the negative and the guilt to do it all the same, because there’s beauty to be found.

caption:
Cycle breaking is wild because one minute you’re validating your kid’s feelings, and the next minute you’re hiding in the pantry trying to regulate yourself, whispering, “No one taught me how to do this shit.” ??

But that IS the work.

Catching yourself, repairing when needed, pausing before automatically repeating what was handed to you. Choosing, over and over again, to build something different - even when it would be easier not to.

Is it messy?? Absolutely.
Is it hard? Some days, unbelievably.
Does it require perfection?? Nope, not even close.

The science has never said kids need perfect parents. Secure attachment is built through rupture AND repair - through moments of disconnection, followed by reconnection. That’s normal, expected, healthy - that’s human.

So if you’re showing up every day, trying to do things with more awareness, more intention, more compassion than what you experienced growing up?? Damn, boo. You’re killing it.

caption:
Stop wasting your time worrying about what other people think. Let Them!

Nobody is thinking about you as much as you think they are.

Daniel Pink is one of the world’s leading experts on human behavior and the author of the largest study on regret ever conducted, analyzing more than 26,000 regrets from people across 134 countries.

Daniel explains that what holds you back isn’t reality, social psychology calls the spotlight effect. You assume other people are watching, judging, and thinking about you far more than they actually are.

But the truth is simple:
People are thinking about themselves.

And the time you spend worrying about what others might think is often the same time you miss opportunities you later wish you had taken.

On this episode of themelrobbinspodcast, danpink breaks down why this belief holds you back, how much power it takes from you, and what happens when you stop worrying and start acting.

Stay tuned - This episode drops Monday, May 25th! ?? “What Makes a Good Life? This Study on 26,000 Regrets Will Guide You for the Rest of Your Life”

What are you doing with the time you’ve been given today?

You can spend it overthinking.
You can spend it comparing.
Or you can spend it actually living your life.

Taking the first step. Making the call. Putting yourself out there. Taking a risk. Slowing down. Enjoying the little moments.

What’s one thing you can do today that matters to YOU? Tell me in the comments ??

When you don’t know where your water will come from, it can show up as worry, frustration, and stress that you carry throughout your entire day.

That’s why we measure more than time or distance. 

Using the Water Insecurity Experiences (WISE) Scale, we track what it actually feels like to live without reliable water.

Because clean water doesn’t just give back time, money, and health.

It also gives back happiness, confidence, and peace of mind.

Thank you to Smile Generation for helping lift the daily weight of water insecurity by bringing clean water to 340,000 people and counting. 

From now until the end of May, Smile Generation offices across the country are raising money for clean water.

caption:
Ladakh sits high in the Himalayas, known as a high altitude desert where mountains stretch for miles and the landscape feels almost otherworldly. Much of the region sits above 3,000 metres, making it one of the highest inhabited areas on Earth.

It’s also home to some of the highest motorable roads in the world, winding through vast valleys, remote villages and dramatic passes that feel completely removed from the rest of the country.

The terrain is dry, open and constantly shifting in colour, from deep browns to soft golds, with bright blue lakes like Pangong adding contrast to the landscape.

Remote, rugged and unlike anywhere else in India, it’s a side of the country that still feels relatively untouched.

BONUS: If you do choose to road trip, here are a few of our favorites ??

1. Zurich to Appenzell for art and culture, 2-3 days, 100 km (62 miles)
2. Appenzell to St Moritz for record-breaking sights, 2-5 days, 290 km (180 miles)
3. St Moritz to Bellinzona for drama, 2-5 days, 290 km (180 miles)
4. Bellinzona to Zermatt for mountain roads, 3-5 days, 520 km (323 miles)
5. Zermatt to Lausanne for postcard-perfect villages, 1-3 days, 260 km (160 miles)

Each year, millions of antelope traverse South Sudan, moving toward permanent water and greener grass during the dry season and spreading out across tens of thousands of square miles when the rains return. For decades, the largest land mammal migration on Earth was masked by the brutal conflict in the region, but the relative peace of recent years has brought new pressures, as people looking to restart their lives are expanding settlements. Nat Geo photographer Marcus Westberg marcuswestbergphotography has filmed this massive migration by drone, and his groundbreaking footage shows the immense scale of this natural wonder.

Babsi (babsi_vigl) has always been fascinated by climbing; it’s also always been about more than summiting (though she has bagged plenty of those, too). Raised in the Austrian Alps, she’s been climbing since she was a child and went on her first expedition at the age of 20. In the years since, she has explored the Himalaya, Patagonia, Yosemite, Alaska and countless other ranges around the world.
 
As impressive as her long list of objectives, however, are all her other roles in the climbing community: She’s also an occupational therapist who specializes in healing injured climbers; an instructor who teaches young mountaineers and mentors women in the alpine, and a professional writer who captures stories that make up the sport she loves.
 
“I think I’m a really curious person, and I feel there’s still so much to discover in my sport,” she says. “Even a route you’ve climbed 100 times, you can go back and find something new: it’s a different season, or you have new skills. Our planet is really big and there are so many places and communities to discover. Too many for one
life.”
 
Excited to do some exploring with you, Babsi. Welcome to the team.

caption:
Remarkable acts of resistance exist all around us, and they always have. Our new book, “Protest,” written by lifelong activists Annie Leonard and Andre Carothers, highlights the formidable and deeply human tradition of peaceful protest, placing today’s threats within a long arc of collective action. We hope this book helps you see yourself in this tradition, and deepens your resolve to act. Buy the book at the link in bio.

Why a book about protest? We don’t have a shot at saving our home planet if we lose the right to protest. It’s this same reason that we offer nonviolent direct action trainings to our employees, give them paid activism hours to engage in peaceful protests, and bail them out of jail if things escalate. With protest under attack across the world, it’s our responsibility to do what we can to protect this human right.

caption:
I’m not going to show you my ugly dance because the whole point is it’s not a performance but seriously - when was the last time you let yourself out of the cage of having to be so fucking palatable all the time?? I think we have generations of witches healers oracles grandmothers behind us urging us to drop the façade and to let our inner witches out. When I’m moving and I’m able to let go completely I sometimes envision my hair turning completely gray, warts growing out of my face, nose hairs long, back crooked… And I just laugh. It’s the best feeling. Being “pretty” is a cage. Fitting in is a cage. Playing small is a cage. For how long have we exhausted ourselves to be beautiful, to be thin, to be acceptable - bending over backwards to not be too much, too loud, to not take up too much space. I’ve spent a lifetime doing that. So when I dance I see Baba Yaga. I see Kali. I feel her. 

In another lifetime I was her!! And I bring her out to play a little bit each time I ugly dance.

You should try it, too?????

#freedom #selfcare #letgo

caption:
#AgonyAli

Should you be friends first before dating? It depends on the intention. 

If you have a crush on someone and your strategy is to become friends first so they see what a great person you are before dropping the bomb that you like them, that feels a little duplicitous. In that situation, just be honest and express your feelings.

But if you genuinely start off as friends and over time both people develop feelings, that's amazing because there wasn't a hidden intention behind it.

It really comes down to this: are you being honest with your intentions or not?

This is also culturally specific. In some cultures, starting as friends is the norm even if both people like each other. There's plausible deniability and it doesn't have to be weird.

What do you think?

My first business started at my dining table ??

????? When I was 18, I decided I could help kids ace the BMAT, which is the medical school entrance exam. My brother was in the year below me at school and had a bunch of friends applying to medical school. So I just messaged them all on Facebook saying I'm running this one-day workshop on how to do well in the BMAT, it's going to be at my house, and it's £50.

Four people signed up. We took out our dining table, extended it, and these four kids sat on chairs around it while I stood by the TV going through my presentation ??

All four of them are doctors now ?? One of them became a consultant neurologist.

The lesson here is that starting small and scrappy is way better than spending ages trying to build the perfect thing before you even validate that people want to pay you for it.

caption:
“Where are you really from?” That's a question Japanese American artist Roger Shimomura has been asked all his life, despite being born and raised in Seattle, Washington. 
 
He and his family were among the more than 120,000 Japanese American people, most of them United States citizens, uprooted and forced into concentration camps during World War II. 

Through his artwork, Shimomura grapples with the challenges of being “different” in America. He creates paintings and performances that blend a mix of Japanese imagery and American pop culture. Often, his playful pop-style paintings feature exaggerated cultural stereotypes. 
 
In “Super Buddahead,” Shimomura adds his own head to the body of Superman, a character who was frequently depicted in combat against stereotypes of German and Japanese soldiers during World War II.

caption:
We remember Jason Collins, who played 13 seasons in the National Basketball Association and opened doors for other professional athletes when he publicly came out as gay in 2013. 
 
At seven feet tall, Collins played center for six NBA teams throughout his career. After the 2012–13 season, he made headlines when he came out in a feature article for Sports Illustrated magazine. Collins became the first openly gay athlete to play in any of the four major North American pro sports leagues when he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2014. 
 
In that Sports Illustrated article, Collins reflected on why it was important to him to 
come out publicly. 
 
“I didn't set out to be the first openly gay athlete playing in a major American team sport. But since I am, I'm happy to start the conversation. I wish I wasn't the kid in the classroom raising his hand and saying, "I'm different." If I had my way, someone else would have already done this. Nobody has, which is why I'm raising my hand.” 
 
Collins’ jersey, signed by the 2013-14 Nets team, is in the collections of our NMAAHC.

AmHistoryMuseum curator Theo Gonzalves took us behind the scenes to learn more about the legacy of Fred Ho, who blended his Chinese American culture with his musical influences in both his compositions and his clothes!
 
“My boots were inspired by my trip to Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom in Cambodia and the Karnak Temple in Luxor, Egypt,” Ho reflected. “Those have been standing at least for millennia. Still vibrant forever. So I feel like anything that we create should be that.”
 
Fred Ho’s boots will be one of the 250 objects on view in our National Museum of American History’s exhibition “In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness,” opening May 14 as part of the museum’s United States 250th anniversary celebrations.

?? Known as the “Godfather of Salsa,” Dominican-born musician and composer Johnny Pacheco (1935-2021) popularized the Latin music genre. 

As the cofounder of salsa’s legendary record label Fania Records in New York City in 1964, Pacheco promoted the term “salsa” as a way of packaging together the different sounds of Afro-Cuban and Afro-Caribbean music. As the label’s musical director and bandleader of the group Fania All Stars, he made music alongside icons like Celia Cruz, Charlie Palmieri, and Pete “El Conde” Rodríguez. While Pacheco’s music often echoed a more traditional Cuban sound, he produced almost 250 albums representing diverse styles within salsa. 

See his 1970s outfit on view in “¡Puro Ritmo! The Musical Journey of Salsa,” presented by the USLatinoMuseum. Featuring hundreds of objects, the exhibition tells the story of salsa and its family of rhythms.

?? Conocido como el “Padrino de la Salsa”, el músico y compositor de origen dominicano Johnny Pacheco (1935-2021) popularizó este género musical latino. 

Como cofundador del legendario sello discográfico de salsa Fania Records, establecido en la ciudad de Nueva York en 1964, Pacheco promovió el término “salsa” como una forma de englobar los diversos sonidos de la música afrocubana y afrocaribeña. En su rol como director musical del sello y líder de la agrupación Fania All Stars, creó música junto a iconos de la talla de Celia Cruz, Charlie Palmieri y Pete “El Conde” Rodríguez. Si bien la música de Pacheco solía evocar un sonido cubano más tradicional, produjo cerca de 250 álbumes que representaban una gran diversidad de estilos dentro del género de la salsa.

Descubre el atuendo que Pacheco lució en la década de 1970, exhibido en “¡Puro Ritmo! The Musical Journey of Salsa”, una exposición presentada por el Museo Nacional del Latino Estadounidense. Esta exposición narra, a través de cientos de objetos, la historia de la salsa y su familia de ritmos.

Captured during a highly active phase, this incredible image by aj.smadi reveals giant sunspots, swirling plasma, and tangled magnetic fields across the Sun’s surface.

These dark regions are areas of intense magnetic activity — some larger than Earth itself — capable of unleashing powerful solar flares and charged particle storms into space.

The same eruptions that create breathtaking auroras on Earth can also interfere with satellites and communication systems.

Our Sun isn’t calm or quiet — it’s a dynamic, constantly changing star at the heart of our solar system.

The relationship between fashion and art has always been enduring. 

This April, AlexConsani appeared as one of the figures who inspired a digital persona created by TomokazuMatsuyama, aka Matsu, for his Midnight Moment in Time’s Square. Throughout the month, every night at midnight, Times Square has illuminated with his work across its iconic screens. On April 10, the project was celebrated with Alex, Matsu, and an intimate gathering in the heart of the city. A rare sight to witness in New York after dark. 

Be sure to see it before its final night on April 30.
